Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this 34-year-old male who attended my practice for evaluation of long-standing back and joint stiffness. He is employed as an accountant, maintains an active lifestyle, and does not smoke. His medical history is non-contributory, and his vital signs and routine blood work were completely unremarkable.

Physical examination demonstrated pronounced dorsal kyphosis accompanied by scoliosis, alongside reduced mobility at both elbows with deficits in terminal extension and flexion. Muscular tone across all extremities was entirely preserved, with no signs of hypotonia. His hands appeared standard; the thumbs were normally proportioned with no spatulate appearance, and there were no joint contractures affecting his hands or digits. Both feet were normally aligned, showing no clubfoot or equinovarus deformities.

Radiographic evaluation revealed severe, generalized flattening of the vertebral bodies throughout the spine, with notable anterior beaked contours. Splaying and flaring of the long-bone metaphyses were clearly evident. Pelvic radiographs showed distinct underdevelopment and hypoplasia of the iliac bodies, accompanied by prominent enlargement and overgrowth of the femoral trochanters bilaterally. The femoral heads appeared well-formed with no dysplastic changes, and the hips were seated securely without dislocation. Finally, wrist films demonstrated age-appropriate skeletal maturity without any advanced ossification among the carpal bones.

Given this presentation, I would value your expert assessment and guidance regarding further diagnostic investigation.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Ward
